director_mandate_binding.note: This spec refines the Director's binding question (request.json#director_mandate) into the smallest rigorous falsifiable measurement. It preserves the frozen claim, the five discovery channels, K=3, threshold 0.50 and the >=2-engine materiality rule. It repairs the v1 (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167) defects: (a) the frozen v1 pool was EMPTY (seeds=[], confirmed_deep_items=[], confirmed_deep_hosts=[] as frozen), so this v2 spec re-derives a live-certified non-empty DEEP frame in DESIGN; (b) the v1 risky composition that v1 DESIGN reconnaissance worried about (two page-level-sitemap candidates vitepress.dev + htmx.org, and an unreachable host www.gnu.org with OSError 101) is replaced by a pool with exactly ONE page-level-sitemap engine, ONE static-search-index engine without content-sitemap subtree coverage, and TWO index-less engines, so the >=2-engine materiality boundary is genuinely at risk through the non-trivial static-index channel.

question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate frozen by EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378, over a frozen 4-engine pool of DEEP (shortest-path hop in {3,4,5,6}) state-carrying items (a page whose HTML contains >=1 named <input>/<select>), what fraction of those items is reachable in <=K=3 fresh-agent GETs (1 discovery GET + 1 item-page GET + 1 spare) via ANY of five frozen site-native discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) -- with preregistered materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 distinct host engines deciding whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (persistent path caching is not a core optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface?

hypothesis.H1: DISCOVERY_COLLAPSES_DEPTH: on >=2 distinct host engines, >=0.50 of admitted DEEP state items are reachable in <=K=3 GETs via at least one frozen site-native discovery channel, so shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier and path/procedure persistence is not the primary optimization target.
hypothesis.H0: DEPTH_REMAINS_BARRIER: on fewer than 2 engines does the per-engine reachable fraction reach 0.50, so even with site-native discovery fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence retains a depth-dependent amortization surface.
hypothesis.note: The experiment does not presuppose which holds. E (decision_rule.engine_count_variable) is not fixed by the frozen frame; no per-item or per-engine reachability witness exists anywhere in this packet, and the per-engine fractions are measured only at EXECUTE.

falsifier.denominator: 40 admitted DEEP state items across 4 distinct host engines (>=10 total, >=3 per engine; exact URL list frozen in target_pool.admitted_items)
falsifier.positive_branch: Let E = number of available host engines with discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine >= 0.50. SUPPORTS iff E >= 2. Then shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition; persistence of paths/procedures is not the primary optimization target.
falsifier.negative_branch: Let E as above. FALSIFIES iff E == 0; E == 1 is reported as the MIXED sub-case. Both belong to the negative branch: even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound on a material share of engines and persistence retains a computable depth-dependent amortization surface.
falsifier.per_channel_disclosure: Mandatory per-channel coverage (discovery_reachable_fraction_per_channel and channels_with_zero_deep) with any channel yielding zero admitted DEEP items listed explicitly rather than counted as a null.
falsifier.why_reachable: E is not fixed by the frozen frame. The frozen record contains NO per-item or per-engine reachability witness; per-engine fractions are determined at EXECUTE by live channel outputs under the frozen parsers. In the assignment space consistent with the frozen frame: SUPPORTS (E>=2) is feasible (the vitepress.dev page-level sitemap channel AND the nix.dev static search-index channel enumerate their frozen items at EXECUTE); the negative branch is feasible via MIXED (E==1: exactly one of those two conjunctions fails, e.g. static-index parser/canonicalization mismatch, doc_urls entry-coverage gaps, redirect/availability drift) and via FALSIFIES (E==0: both fail, e.g. robots/sitemap blocking or re-organization). No frozen fact rules out any of the three outcome assignments. Structural honesty (measured at DESIGN): per-engine site-native discovery on this documentation-engine class is close to deterministic in whether the engine publishes a machine-readable content index (page-level content sitemap or static search index): the one page-level-sitemap engine (vitepress.dev: ROBOTS_SITEMAP/SITEMAP_XML both 272 locs) and the one static-search-index engine (nix.dev mdBook searchindex.js: 1933 doc_urls) return non-empty URL sets, while the two index-less engines return ZERO URL output from every channel (doc.rust-lang.org: robots.txt -> sitemap.txt with only the 3 version roots, /sitemap.xml 404; rust-lang.github.io: no robots.txt, no sitemap.xml, no search index, no feed, no JSON-LD). The pool is therefore deliberately composed as exactly ONE page-level engine + ONE static-index engine + TWO index-less engines: the materiality boundary E>=2 is genuinely at risk through the NON-TRIVIAL ON_SITE_SEARCH static-index channel and is NOT guaranteed by a second trivially-covering engine, and the two index-less engines exert the measured negative floor. The design deliberately does NOT include a per-item reachability witness (which would pre-prove the outcome).

B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS.description: Frozen item-blind same-host document-order link-following BFS (RED arm of EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378): the number of HTTP GET requests issued before an admitted item page is first fetched, and its hop depth.
B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS.identifiable: Computed at EXECUTE on the SAME frozen admitted item set by re-running the frozen BFS (B=250, D=6, same-host static-<a>, document order) once per seed; deterministic on a stable site, with temporal drift recorded. The DESIGN-time BFS that constructed the frame used the same frozen policy.

B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY.role: theoretical O(1) lower bound when the item URL is already known
B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY.description: One GET to the already-known item page URL (RACQ_URL of EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378).

B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.role: contextual (NOT a comparator in the primary decision)
B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.description: Persisted shortest-path replay cost hop+1 measured in the parent EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 on a single-engine mdBook pool. Recorded as inherited context only; it is explicitly NOT re-measured here and is not used to compute the primary metric.
B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.identifiable: Analytically defined; labeled inherited context; never paired with this experiment's discovery metric.

positive_control.description: At least one frozen site-native discovery channel must be probeable and return parsable same-host URL content (a non-empty parsed same-host URL set) on at least one host in the frozen pool, verified live during DESIGN.
positive_control.pass_criterion: At least one of the five channels yields a 2xx response whose parsed same-host URL set is non-empty on at least one host; verified in pre_freeze_control_certificate.channel_liveness.
positive_control.aggregate_only_note: This control is INSTRUMENT liveness only and is reported AGGREGATELY: per-host channel URL-set sizes (272/272 for vitepress.dev sitemaps, 58/58 for nix.dev sitemaps, 3 for doc.rust-lang.org robots->sitemap.txt, 1933 doc_urls for nix.dev searchindex.js, 0 for every channel on rust-lang.github.io). DESIGN deliberately does NOT compute, and the certificate deliberately does NOT contain, any per-item or per-engine reachability witness. A per-item witness (v1-era PC_KNOWN_DEEP_ITEM_WITNESS_BOUNDED) was REMOVED because it pre-computed which engines cross threshold and thereby made E foregone; the confirmatory per-engine fractions are measured only at EXECUTE.
positive_control.observed_pre_freeze: Aggregate channel liveness as verified on 2026-10-10 (this re-run of DESIGN): ROBOTS_SITEMAP non-empty on vitepress.dev (272 locs), nix.dev (58 locs), doc.rust-lang.org (3 lines via sitemap.txt; robots.txt 200); SITEMAP_XML non-empty on vitepress.dev (272), nix.dev (58); ON_SITE_SEARCH non-empty URL set on nix.dev (mdBook searchindex.js parsed as text, 1933 doc_urls); RSS_ATOM 0 and JSON_LD 0 on all four seed roots; rust-lang.github.io returns ZERO URL output from every channel (no robots.txt, no sitemap, no search index; all well-known probes 404).

null_control.description: Per host, two frozen synthetic identifiers that do not exist are probed through the parsed URL sets of the discovery channels and by direct item-page fetch. They must yield zero discovered URLs and 404 on the item page, across all hosts.
null_control.pass_criterion: For all hosts and channels: 0 synthetic URLs discovered AND every synthetic item page returns 404.
null_control.purpose: Validates that the channels/parsers do not manufacture false-positive reachability via stale entries, redirects, parser errors or fuzzy matching (the flip side of representation loss: no false accepts).

NC_SYNTHETIC_SITEMAP_ABSENCE.expected: synthetic URLs absent from every parsed sitemap/search-index URL set on every host
NC_SYNTHETIC_SITEMAP_ABSENCE.pre_freeze_observed: absent on all 4 hosts (synthetic ids not found in vitepress sitemap/hashmap, nix.dev sitemap/doc_urls, doc.rust-lang.org sitemap.txt, rust-lang.github.io absence)

NC_SYNTHETIC_PAGE_404.expected: every synthetic item page returns HTTP 404
NC_SYNTHETIC_PAGE_404.pre_freeze_observed: 404 on all 8 synthetic probes (2 per host x 4 hosts), re-certified 2026-10-10

operational_definitions.substrate: HTTP GET only via Python stdlib urllib; TLS verified; frozen User-Agent 'SPIDER-research-frontier-38013774272/1.0'; timeout 12s; max response body 600000 bytes (one exception below); redirects followed; no credentials, cookies, browser, Docker, model key or write verb. EXCEPTION: mdBook searchindex.js and sitemap artifacts are fetched with a 12000000-byte cap where needed (nix.dev searchindex.js measured 8.6 MB at DESIGN).
operational_definitions.navigation_graph: Directed graph whose nodes are canonicalized same-host http(s) URLs and whose edges are static <a href> links parsed in document order; asset extensions excluded; JS-generated links are NOT edges (disclosed VN-V2).
operational_definitions.hop_distance: Graph shortest-path length in edges from the seed root (hop 0), measured by the frozen BFS (budget B=250, depth cap D=6, each URL fetched at most once).
operational_definitions.state_carrying_item: A page that contains >=1 named form control: <input> with non-empty name attribute OR <select> with non-empty name attribute. The item observable is the page URL; named_controls is recorded per item.
operational_definitions.DEEP: hop in {3,4,5,6} (inherited from the parent's DEEP band; state items at hop<=2 are outside the frame).
operational_definitions.canonicalization: Two distinct notions, both frozen: (a) ITEM URL FORM = the engine-native serving form as stored in target_pool.admitted_items (extensionless on vitepress.dev, nix.dev, rust-lang.github.io; '.html' on doc.rust-lang.org where extensionless returns 404). EXECUTE fetches the stored form. (b) CANONICAL MATCH KEY = final URL after redirects; fragment removed, query string removed, trailing slash removed, terminal '.html'/'.htm' removed from the last path segment; applied identically to item URLs and to every channel-output URL before matching (so a search-index entry 'command-ref/nix-copy-closure.html#...' matches item '.../command-ref/nix-copy-closure').

channel_definitions.ROBOTS_SITEMAP: GET https://<host>/robots.txt; extract Sitemap: directive URLs; GET each sitemap (gzip-decoded if .gz); if a sitemapindex, recurse into up to 12 child sitemaps; union all <loc> and plain-text URL entries; match the item's canonical match key.
channel_definitions.SITEMAP_XML: GET https://<host>/sitemap.xml and https://<host>/sitemap_index.xml directly (same recursion/gzip rules) and match. NOTE: doc.rust-lang.org returns 404 for both (only robots.txt routes to its sitemap.txt); this is a measured per-host fact, recorded in pre_freeze_control_certificate.channel_liveness.
channel_definitions.ON_SITE_SEARCH: Two sub-mechanisms, both without JS execution: (a) STATIC FORM branch: on the seed root locate a static <form> that has an EXPLICIT action attribute and a named search-like input; construct action?param=<item last path segment>; GET results; match item URLs. Forms WITHOUT an explicit action attribute (e.g., mdBook 'searchbar-outer' forms on nix.dev/doc.rust-lang.org/rust-lang.github.io, whose default action is the page itself) are NOT invoked and yield zero output; this is a measured aggregate instrument fact. (b) STATIC INDEX branch: probe well-known static search-index artifacts referenced from or well-known relative to the seed root and parse them WITHOUT EXECUTING JS: JSON indexes (/search/search_index.json, /search-index.json, /search.json, /pagefind/pagefind-entry.json, /hashmap.json) AND JS-wrapped static index-data files whose payload is a literal JSON object/array (notably mdBook /searchindex.js containing a 'doc_urls' array). For mdBook searchindex.js the doc_urls entries are RESOLVED against the directory of the artifact (e.g., https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/ + 'command-ref/nix-copy-closure.html#...') before canonicalization. Windows of URL/non-URL artifacts are recorded as measured facts (e.g., vitepress.dev /hashmap.json is present with 282 keys but its keys are '.md'-relative ids, NOT URLs, so it yields zero URL entries under the match rule). This static-.js extension is REQUIRED for two-sidedness: without it, mdBook content pages that have no content-sitemap coverage are undiscoverable by construction, which would manufacture a floor (a v1 defect). Any executed-JS or remote query endpoint (API search, Algolia, pagefind JS loader) is NOT invoked (disclosed).
channel_definitions.RSS_ATOM: Find <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml|application/atom+xml> on the seed root; GET the feed; match item URLs from <item><link>, <entry><link href> or <guid>. Measured at DESIGN: zero feed alternate links on all four seed roots.
channel_definitions.JSON_LD: GET the seed root as a discovery hub and enumerate same-host URLs from all <script type=application/ld+json> blocks (url/@id/mainEntityOfPage/itemListElement). ANTI-TAUTOLOGY: the item page itself is NOT used as its own JSON-LD hub (a self-fetch implementation is rejected). Measured at DESIGN: zero ld+json blocks on all four seed roots.

operational_definitions.channel_success_rule: A channel succeeds for an item iff the item's canonical match key is discovered from that channel's output AND the item page is fetched with a final 2xx within the remaining K GETs. Each 3xx redirect counts as 1 GET.
operational_definitions.union_rule: item_reachable_via_discovery = OR(channel_success over the 5 channels); each channel is probed independently per fresh episode (no cross-item caching), so an item's reachability is certified within its own K=3 episode.
operational_definitions.sampling_rule: Frozen frame = for each seed, run the frozen BFS once (budget 250, depth 6, same-host static-<a>, document order); admit text/html pages at hop in {3,4,5,6} with >=1 named control; within an engine admit up to 10 items in BFS fetch order (first-10 rule). Deterministic; the exact admitted URL list with engine-native serving forms is frozen in target_pool.admitted_items (40 items, 10 per engine).
operational_definitions.temporal_drift: EXECUTE measures discovery on the exact frozen admitted item URLs and re-runs the frozen BFS only to record hop depth and requests-to-first-reach; an admitted URL that no longer resolves at EXECUTE is excluded with a recorded reason and its exclusion reported. Frame drift is a disclosed validity threat.

measurement_validity.VN-V1_substrate: Credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP; no browser, Docker, model key, credential, cookie or write verb. Identical to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378.
measurement_validity.VN-V2_static_parser_only: HTML parsed with stdlib html.parser/regex. JS-rendered navigation and JS-executed search are NOT followed, so JS-dependent discovery channels are missed and disclosed as representation loss. Static JS-wrapped index DATA files are parsed as text without executing JS (see ON_SITE_SEARCH).
measurement_validity.VN-V3_same_host: Only same-host static navigation defines hop; cross-host navigation is out of scope, which bounds the claim to same-host acquisition on this substrate class.
measurement_validity.VN-V4_frame_certificate: The DEEP state-item frame was certified live during DESIGN across 4 distinct host engines (40 items, 10 per engine): every admitted URL returned final 2xx with the recorded named_controls on 2026-10-10, and hop=3 for all 40 (the shallow member of the DEEP band). Pinned inline in target_pool.admitted_items (hashed inside spec.json by the freezer).
measurement_validity.VN-V5_k_budget: K=3 includes redirects and item-page fetch; it is generous for the measured channel mechanics: sitemap channels need robots+sitemap+item (3 GETs) or sitemap+item (2), the static-index branch needs seed+index+item (3), feeds need root+feed+item (3).
measurement_validity.VN-V6_channel_independence: Channels are probed independently and reported separately; overlap (e.g., robots.txt -> sitemap) is disclosed and the union is not double-counted per item.
measurement_validity.VN-V7_no_token_cost: No tokenizer/latency/dollar model; GET requests and response-body bytes are the only cost bases; token fields are null.
measurement_validity.VN-V8_selection_bias: The frozen pool is a purposive sample of public documentation engines that pass the depth+control frame gate, not a random Web sample. The metric is explicitly conditional on these engines; generalization beyond the admitted pool is not claimed.
measurement_validity.VN-V9_bimodality_disclosure: Measured at DESIGN: on this documentation-engine class, per-engine site-native discovery is close to a deterministic function of whether the engine publishes a machine-readable content index (page-level content sitemap OR static search index): vitepress.dev (272 sitemap locs) and nix.dev (1933 doc_urls) yield non-empty URL sets; doc.rust-lang.org (sitemap.txt with only 3 version roots, /sitemap.xml 404) and rust-lang.github.io (no robots/sitemap/index/feed/JSON-LD) yield zero. The pool is deliberately composed as exactly ONE page-level-sitemap engine, ONE static-search-index engine, and TWO index-less engines, so that the >=2-engine boundary is genuinely at risk (concentrated on the single non-trivial ON_SITE_SEARCH static-index mechanism on nix.dev) and is NOT guaranteed by a second trivially-covering engine. The known cost of this composition is reduced power to detect intermediate per-engine fractions and a tight dynamic range on E (ex-ante expectation E in {1,2}); this is disclosed as the central validity threat. The that-matters discrimination is: does the ONLY mechanism that can move the boundary (a static search index on an engine with no content-sitemap subtree coverage) actually enumerate the frozen DEEP items at EXECUTE?
measurement_validity.VN-V10_sitemap_recursion_cap: sitemapindex recursion is capped at 12 child sitemaps and URL parsing at 20000 URLs per host to bound bytes; a host exceeding the cap is recorded with the cap hit.
measurement_validity.VN-V11_temporal_drift: Live hosts can change between DESIGN and EXECUTE; the frozen URL list is measured as-is and drift is recorded rather than silently re-sampled.
measurement_validity.VN-V12_availability: If a seed host is unreachable at EXECUTE, that engine is recorded as unavailable (excluded from E with reason); network failure is never encoded as a scientific negative.
measurement_validity.VN-V13_cross_subtree_items: The doc.rust-lang.org seed (/book/) reaches sibling rust docs (/cargo/, root) at hop>=3 via the shared top navigation; these are retained as legitimate same-host DEEP state items and their cross-subtree origin is disclosed. The rust-lang.github.io seed (/async-book/) similarly reaches sibling projects (/rfcs/, /wg-async/); disclosed.
measurement_validity.VN-V14_item_url_forms: Item URLs are stored in engine-native serving forms and fetched as-is: extensionless on vitepress.dev, nix.dev and rust-lang.github.io; '.html' on doc.rust-lang.org (extensionless returns 404 there). Matching always uses the canonical match key (fragment/query/slash/'.html' stripped) applied identically to items and channel outputs, so search-index '.html' entries match extensionless items and vice versa.

decision_rule.primary_decision_variable: E = count over engines available at EXECUTE of (discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine[host] >= threshold). E is the sole variable that maps to an outcome; the aggregate discovery_reachable_fraction and the per-channel fractions are reported diagnostics and are NOT themselves the decision variable.
decision_rule.primary_metric: discovery_reachable_fraction = count(admitted DEEP items with item_reachable_via_discovery=true) / count(admitted DEEP items)
decision_rule.engine_count_variable: E = number of host engines with discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine >= threshold among engines that are available at EXECUTE

outcome_mapping.MIXED: E == 1 (sub-case of the negative/materiality boundary; reported distinctly for mechanism localization)
outcome_mapping.INCONCLUSIVE: admission gate fails (pool < 10 admitted DEEP items total or fewer than 2 engines with >= 3 admitted DEEP items available) or a pre-registered measurement-validity gate fails

decision_rule.materiality_boundary: The preregistered materiality boundary is E >= 2. SUPPORTS requires E >= 2; both MIXED (E==1) and FALSIFIES (E==0) belong to the negative branch (depth remains an acquisition barrier).

admission_gate.on_failure: status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID/INCONCLUSIVE with the exact shortfall; no scientific branch is reported.

decision_rule.per_channel_reporting: Mandatory per-channel coverage for all 5 channels, with any channel yielding zero admitted DEEP items listed explicitly.
decision_rule.controls_observed_rule: If PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_LIVENESS fails at EXECUTE, or either null sub-control fires, the run is status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID and no branch is scored.

product_consequence_positive: If SUPPORTS (E>=2): shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier where a machine-readable content index (content sitemap or static search index) exists; persistent path caches are not the primary optimization target for SPIDER memory; effort shifts to discovery-channel coverage, engine/index-artifact detection, hybrid discovery+traversal for uncovered engines, and substrate expansion. C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY's 'pay for novelty, not the whole task' thesis is supported for the acquisition phase when such an index is available.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIES/MIXED (E<2): even with the full frozen site-native discovery toolkit, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound on a material share of engines (the two measured index-less engines exert the floor); persistence of paths/procedures retains a real depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from measured re-derivation cost; memory architecture should keep investing in persistence with freshness guards and delta repair, and Frontier should improve discovery recall or adopt hybrid strategies.

estimated_cost.http_gets_estimate: ~1400-1900 GETs total: hop-confirmation BFS 4x250=1000 + discovery probing 40 items x 5 channels x <=3 GETs (~600 worst case but typically 40x2=80 for sitemap engines) + channel hub/robot/sitemap/search-index fetches (~20, incl. nix.dev searchindex.js 8.6 MB and vitepress hashmap.json) + null control 8 x 2 + frame re-certification. nix.dev searchindex.js is fetched once per ON_SITE_SEARCH episode per item under the no-cross-item-caching rule (up to 10 fetches x 8.6 MB).
estimated_cost.compute_cost: Negligible CPU/RAM (stdlib HTTP + parsing); ~1-2 GB worst-case transfer if all 10 nix.dev index episodes occur (10 x 8.6 MB).
estimated_cost.external_dependencies: Public HTTP endpoints only; no API keys, credentials or rate-limited APIs.

expected_information_gain: High and decision-changing for the program-level architecture synthesis. The experiment measures, on a live-certified multi-engine DEEP frame, whether site-native discovery collapses the depth cost that motivates SPIDER's persistence architecture. SUPPORTS redirects the program from path persistence to discovery/substrate expansion; FALSIFIES/MIXED validates persistence and yields a real break-even surface. Per-engine and per-channel reporting localizes the mechanism (sitemap granularity, static-index availability, feed/JSON-LD absence) rather than reporting a single average. Even a near-foregone SUPPORTS is decision-relevant because it fences WHERE the claim holds (index-bearing engines) and certifies WHERE it fails (the measured index-less floor).

decision_rule_reachability.reason: Denominator is non-zero and fixed: 40 admitted DEEP state items across 4 engines (>=10 total, >=3 per engine), frozen inline in target_pool.admitted_items (all 40 re-certified 200 + named controls on 2026-10-10). The two-sided rule is computable and all three outcome assignments are live on the frozen frame: no per-item/per-engine witness exists in the frozen record, and E is determined at EXECUTE by live channel outputs. Assignment space: SUPPORTS (E>=2) requires the vitepress page-level sitemap channel AND the nix.dev static-index channel to enumerate their frozen items; MIXED (E==1) requires exactly one of those conjunctions to fail (static-index parser/canonicalization mismatch, entry-coverage gaps, drift); FALSIFIES (E==0) requires both to fail. The pool contains exactly ONE page-level-sitemap engine, ONE static-search-index engine and TWO index-less engines, so the E>=2 boundary is genuinely at risk through the non-trivial mechanism and is not guaranteed by a second trivially-covering engine. Bimodality and the resulting tight dynamic range are disclosed in VN-V9 and falsifier.why_reachable rather than hidden.

measurement_prerequisites.reason: All prerequisites satisfied and executed live during DESIGN on the FINAL pool: credential-free GET-only stdlib substrate works (all four seeds return 2xx with 400+ byte bodies over TLS); the DEEP state-item frame passes the gate on 4 hosts (10 items each, 40 total; each admitted URL re-fetched 200 with recorded named_controls); the 5 channels are fully defined including static .js search-index parsing and its doc_urls resolution rule; channel liveness measured per host (sitemap channels non-empty on 3 hosts, zero on rust-lang.github.io; ON_SITE_SEARCH non-empty on nix.dev); the null control re-run live (8/8 synthetic pages 404, 0 synthetic ids present in any parsed URL set). The v1 problematic hosts (www.gnu.org, unreachable in the v1 environment, and the second page-level-sitemap candidate htmx.org) are not referenced anywhere in this spec's pool.

baseline_identifiability.reason: The within-experiment baseline B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS (hop_depth and bfs_requests_to_first_reach) is computable on the SAME frozen admitted item set under the frozen BFS policy re-run once per seed at EXECUTE, and was the exact policy that constructed the frame at DESIGN. B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY is the constant 1 GET by construction. B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT is analytically defined and explicitly labeled inherited context, never paired with this experiment's discovery metric. Identifiers are stable for EXECUTE/AUDIT reuse.

control_sensitivity.reason: Controls are non-tautological and can fire in both directions. NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM fires if a channel/parser manufactures false reachability (pre-freeze: 0 discovered, 404 on all 8 synthetic probes). PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_LIVENESS fires if channels/parsers break at EXECUTE or if robots/sitemap behavior changes (e.g., bot-blocking tomorrow would flip non-empty to empty). The channel set is discriminative on the pool rather than constant: two hosts return zero for every channel (doc.rust-lang.org flagging only 3 version roots; rust-lang.github.io nothing), while the other two return large non-empty sets (272/272; 58/58; 1933 doc_urls) — so the instruments distinguish 'channel absent' from 'channel present but non-matching', and the per-item witness that would have pre-proved the outcome has been removed.

treatment_liveness.reason: The treatment (5-channel site-native discovery probing, including static .js search-index parsing and doc_urls resolution) is executable on the frozen pool using the stdlib GET substrate with no browser/Docker/model key, and was actually exercised in DESIGN on the final pool: robots.txt parsed on all hosts usable (200 on vitepress.dev/nix.dev/doc.rust-lang.org; 404 on rust-lang.github.io), sitemaps parsed (272/272 vitepress.dev, 58/58 nix.dev, 3 via doc.rust-lang.org robots->sitemap.txt, 404 on rust-lang.github.io), nix.dev searchindex.js parsed as text (1933 doc_urls), vitepress hashmap.json parsed (282 non-URL keys), feed-link and JSON-LD scans run (zero everywhere), mdBook form action-attribute characterization run (no explicit action). No treatment arm is structurally incapable of being EXECUTABLE.

freeze_artifacts_bound.reason: No separate mutable local code/data/task-bank/fixture file exists at DESIGN time and none is created (DESIGN scope is spec.json and prereg.md only). The complete sampling frame (seed list + exact admitted DEEP item URLs with engine-native serving forms, hops and named-control counts) is materialized inline in spec.json#target_pool.admitted_items, and all channel/decision definitions are in prereg.md; the deterministic freezer records the SHA-256 of request.json, spec.json, prereg.md and design_review.json in freeze.json.hashes, so the frame and decision rule are identity-bound by the frozen packet. EXECUTE derives its implementation verbatim from the frozen prereg and must publish its code + raw logs as result artifacts; no unbound mutable artifact can change the interpretation of the frozen decision rule. NOTE on the parent-handoff dependency (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167 handoff.dependencies[0](d), which asked that 'pool/crawl/certificate artifacts' be hashed into freeze.json.artifact_hashes): that intent is satisfied here by CONSTRUCTION rather than by a separate artifact, because the pool (all 40 URLs), the live certificate and its probe evidence are inline fields of spec.json and therefore hashed into freeze.json.hashes as part of the canonical spec; there is no separate mutable file whose identity could drift. research/EXPERIMENT_PACKET.md section 2 lines 50-51 explicitly provides that when no mutable local dependency exists, freeze_artifacts_bound must be NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason and freeze_artifacts must be empty. EXECUTE's own freshly written code and raw logs are EXECUTE outputs (result artifacts), not DESIGN-time mutable dependencies, and cannot change the frozen decision rule.
